inputs.share_count_basis: 753,445,230 issued ordinary shares excluding treasury, SIP and EBT holdings at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 results deck, basic EPS basis) plus c.2.9m dilutive share-incentive instruments (FY2025 note 10: diluted 28.0p vs basic 28.1p on 772.4m weighted basic). Held FLAT: SBC incl. NI is fully expensed in the flows, so buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, not an extra source of value. Rightmove has repurchased ~45% of its issued shares since IPO (c.£141m in FY2025, 21.4m shares cancelled) and has guided c.£330m of buybacks in the 12 months to July 2027; that pace exceeds SBC and will shrink the count further, which is value-neutral at a fair price and not credited here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: cash-flow add-back 'Share-based payments' GBP8,539k (line 6337); company's combined 'Share-based payments charges' including related National Insurance GBP9.8m in the underlying operating profit reconciliation (line 1364). UK awards are settled from treasury/EBT shares with no net-share-settlement tax; EquityAwardTaxes = 0, the NI charge is the analogous cash cost and is inside the 9.8m used.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to quote pence; it is a fixed unit conversion, not a market rate, so no date or parity check applies. No dual listing exists for Rightmove.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: UK 10y gilt c.4.5% risk-free, 5.0% UK equity risk premium, beta c.0.9 for a dominant subscription classifieds platform with 25 years of resilient cash generation -> cost of equity c.9.0%. Capital structure is effectively all-equity (GBP200m RCF signed July 2026 is <6% of market cap and undrawn at the last balance sheet), so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: competition, housing cyclicality and regulatory risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Total lease cash outflow (FY2025: GBP3,388k = GBP3,146k principal + GBP80k interest + GBP162k short-term/low-value) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.8% of revenue; lease liabilities (GBP7.2m at 31 Dec 2025) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 depreciation GBP3,937k less ROU depreciation GBP2,583k plus amortisation GBP4,391k = GBP5,745k = 1.35% of revenue. Note last_fcf follows the contract identity (reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income = 213.7); the forward build additionally charges the c.GBP3.4m lease cash, so year-1 owner FCF sits c.GBP3m below a naive roll-forward of last_fcf. Reported FCF (OCF less capex) is flattered by exactly that lease principal, which IFRS 16 parks in financing.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Rightmove has no minority interests; 100% of profit is attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, probability-weighted three scenarios. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US' (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md parts a, b, e, f). Rightmove is a pure B2B subscription marketplace: ~19,300 advertisers paying monthly membership fees, c.72% underlying EBITDA margin, capex c.2.4% of revenue, all surplus cash returned. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. ANCHORS: price is the 2026-10-09 regular close; net cash is the 31 Dec 2025 balance sheet (cash GBP37,223k + money-market deposits GBP5,683k, no borrowings) because the H1 2026 results exist in this folder only as the presentation deck, whose cash bridge is a chart image with no extractable figures; the share count is the deck's 30 June 2026 figure. The vintage mismatch is small for Rightmove (cash is held near GBP35-45m every year-end because everything else is returned) but should be refreshed from the H1 2026 interim statements when they are extracted. The GBP200m RCF (SONIA+1%, matures July 2029) was agreed in July 2026 to part-fund >GBP400m of capital returns over the 12 months to July 2027; management guides c.GBP1m net interest cost in H2 2026 and GBP6-10m in 2027, implying GBP100-200m drawn. Net cash will therefore flip to net debt of up to c.GBP150m by the next update, matched by a lower share count; at a fair price that is value-neutral and is deliberately not pre-empted here. INTEREST INCOME (GBP2.6m) is stripped from the FCF base even though net cash is below the 1x rule of thumb, because the cash pile is added to EV and the matching-asset rule says its income must then leave the flows; the effect is <1% of value. DIGITAL SERVICES TAX: payable at 2% of eligible UK revenues above a GBP25m allowance once annual revenues exceed GBP500m; the base case crosses GBP500m in FY2028 (year 3), so the EBITDA margin path steps down c.1.9pp from year 3 (c.GBP10m) and the bull case crosses in FY2027. The bear case never crosses GBP500m within the horizon. FY2026 exceptional costs of GBP4-7m (guided) are treated as a year-1 cash cost (c.1.2pp of margin), not excluded. SBC: Rightmove's share-based charge is small (2.3% of revenue incl. NI) but has grown faster than revenue (1.6% FY2023 -> 2.3% FY2025) with AI/engineering hiring; held at 2.3% in base, declining to 2.0% in bull, 2.5% flat in bear. Buyback_cash 141.1m is the FY2025 financing-statement 'Purchase of own shares for cancellation', not the authorisation; the flat count is being funded, with a large margin to spare. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside; the house/street band is narrow because SBC is only c.4.5% of owner FCF.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance midpoint (+6-8%, cut from +8-10% in July 2026 on New Homes volumes) cross-checked against the 3yr revenue CAGR (8.5%, FY2022-25) and the COVID-neutral 6yr CAGR (6.6%, FY2019-25). Equity CAGR is not a usable growth proxy for Rightmove: book equity is c.GBP80m on a GBP3.7bn market cap because every pound of surplus cash is returned, so it carries no information about earning power.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-7.8%) diverges from revenue (15.6%) and EPS (17.3%) by far more than 30%, but all three 5yr figures are artefacts: the FY2020 base is the COVID year in which Rightmove gave c.GBP90m of partner discounts (revenue -29%) and suspended the dividend (equity spiked to GBP123m). The 3yr and 6yr series are the ones to read. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (4.1%) is below reported FCF (5.0%): SBC+NI grew from GBP5.9m to GBP9.8m over FY2023-25, so an increasing share of reported growth is being paid in stock, though the absolute amounts remain small.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - cash-flow SBC add-back - interest income: FY2020 90.6, FY2022 190.7, FY2025 215.0 (GBPm). Revenue: FY2019 289.3, FY2020 205.7, FY2022 332.6, FY2025 425.1. EPS (GBP): FY2020 0.126, FY2022 0.234, FY2025 0.280. Equity: FY2020 123.1, FY2022 68.2, FY2025 82.3.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the 6-8% guidance midpoint (H1 was +7%); FY2027 holds 7% as ARPA (+GBP110-120/yr) and Strategic Growth Areas (+20-30%) offset flat New Homes volumes; growth then fades 0.5pp/yr toward 3% as ARPA increases meet agent pushback and membership stays flat. Margin: FY2026 underlying operating profit +3-5% on +7% revenue plus GBP4-7m exceptionals gives c.69% EBITDA (pre-SBC/pre-lease); recovers to 70% in FY2027; steps down 1.9pp in FY2028 when revenue passes GBP500m and the 2% Digital Services Tax applies, then holds 68.5% -- consistent with management's >=67% underlying operating margin floor. Capex 3% through the GBP60m 2026-28 AI programme, then 2.5%. Cash tax at the 25% UK rate.

bull.narrative: FY2026 lands at the top of guidance (8%) and New Homes volumes recover from FY2027 as UK rates fall and housebuilder site openings normalise; Strategic Growth Areas (Commercial, Mortgages, Rental Services) compound at 25-30% and reach c.15% of revenue; AI products (Opportunity Manager, Online Agent Valuation) lift ARPA above GBP120/yr; CoStar/OnTheMarket fails to dent the 80%+ time-share and retention stays at 95%+. Revenue crosses GBP500m in FY2027, so the DST is absorbed a year earlier, but operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base rebuilds EBITDA margin to 72% by FY2032. SBC drifts down to 2.0% as the AI hiring wave matures.

bear.narrative: FY2026 scrapes the bottom of guidance (6%), then CoStar's multi-year OnTheMarket spend (plus a possible OnTheMarket-Zoopla combination) forces Rightmove to defend share with marketing and ARPA restraint: membership slips, ARPA growth stalls, revenue flat by FY2029. The DMCCA/CMA imposes conduct requirements on package pricing. New Homes stays at record-low site openings. Margin compresses from 72% to 60% EBITDA as marketing, AI investment and retention discounts are spent against a flat revenue line -- below management's 67% floor, which is the point of the scenario. Revenue never reaches GBP500m within the horizon so no DST. Terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap reflect a share-losing incumbent. The business remains profitable and cash-generative throughout; this is a de-rating, not a solvency, case.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-midpoint FY2026 (+7%), 7% in FY2027 from ARPA and Strategic Growth Areas against flat New Homes, fading to 3% by year 10. Underlying operating margin dips in FY2026 (profit +3-5% on +7% revenue, plus GBP4-7m exceptionals), recovers in FY2027, then absorbs the 2% Digital Services Tax from FY2028 when revenue passes GBP500m, holding c.68.5% EBITDA thereafter above management's 67% floor. CoStar/OnTheMarket remains a cost (marketing, product investment) rather than a share loss. Capex 3% through the AI programme then 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Top-of-guidance FY2026, New Homes recovery from FY2027 as mortgage rates fall, Strategic Growth Areas at 25-30% reaching c.15% of revenue, AI products lifting ARPA, retention held at 95%+. Operating leverage rebuilds EBITDA margin to 72% by FY2032 even after the DST. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: CoStar-funded price and marketing competition plus DMCCA conduct requirements stall ARPA growth and cost membership; revenue flat by FY2029 and EBITDA margin compresses to 60% as Rightmove spends to defend share. New Homes does not recover. Terminal growth 2%, 15x cap. Still profitable and cash-generative; a de-rating case, not a distress case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because CoStar's backing of OnTheMarket is the first institutionally-funded assault on Rightmove's position in its history, the company itself lists low entry barriers as a principal risk, the DMCCA gives the CMA a live lever over a platform with >80% share, and FY2026 guidance has already been cut once. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: a New Homes volume recovery, Strategic Growth Areas scaling to a material share, and competition staying muted while Rightmove keeps pushing ARPA. Base stays at 50%: the 96% H1 2026 agency retention and 25 years of resilient subscription revenue through every UK housing cycle make continuity the single most likely path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Rightmove is valued as a mature, dominant subscription marketplace: a 10-year owner-FCF build (SBC incl. NI expensed, interest income stripped, leases charged as operating cost, share count flat) discounted at a GBP-built 9% and capitalised at the lower of Gordon (2.5%) and 20x. The question the model asks is not whether Rightmove grows, but how much of its 72% margin survives a well-funded challenger and a UK digital-platform regulator over the next decade; that is why the scenarios diverge on margin far more than on growth, and why bear carries 25%. Buybacks funded by the new RCF are treated as value-neutral at fair value and not credited.
key_risks_to_valuation: CoStar/OnTheMarket (and a possible OnTheMarket-Zoopla combination) turning from a marketing cost into actual membership or ARPA loss -- the bear case margin path
DMCCA / CMA conduct requirements constraining package pricing or bundling for a platform with >80% share of time spent
New Homes volumes failing to recover (developments at a record-low new-to-market rate in H1 2026; FY2026 guided -6% to -10%)
Digital Services Tax from c.FY2028 (c.GBP10m, 1.9pp of margin) -- in the base and bull paths; its abolition would add c.3% to value
AI answer-engines disintermediating portal search (currently <0.5% of traffic from LLM referrals)
Net-cash-to-net-debt transition: up to GBP200m RCF drawn to fund buybacks; value-neutral at fair price but removes the balance-sheet cushion that supported the historical multiple
Balance-sheet anchor is 31 Dec 2025 against a 30 June 2026 share count; refresh when the H1 2026 interim statements are extracted
